requirements.quote: After reviewing the generated script, click Accept Change to apply it to the pre-request script section of your API request.
requirements.statement: User can review the generated pre-request script and click Accept Change to apply it to the pre-request script section.

requirements.quote: Click the Modify with AI icon ( .⟡+ ) within the Pre-request Script section.
requirements.statement: User can click the Modify with AI icon within the Pre-request Script section to generate a pre-request script.

requirements.quote: Click the Modify with AI icon ( .⟡+ ) in the Request Body section.
requirements.statement: User can click the Modify with AI icon in the Request Body section to generate a request body.

requirements.quote: Click the Modify with AI icon ( .⟡+ ) in the Tests section.
requirements.statement: User can click the Modify with AI icon in the Tests section to generate test scripts.

requirements.quote: Create mock servers in Hoppscotch to simulate API endpoints with custom responses, status codes, and latency for prototyping and testing.
requirements.statement: User can create mock servers in Hoppscotch that simulate API endpoints with custom responses, status codes, and latency.

requirements.quote: You can create a mock server from scratch or from an existing Collection.
requirements.section: API Mocking > Create a mock server
requirements.statement: User can create a mock server from scratch or from an existing Collection.

requirements.quote: Once created, you'll get a mock server URL you can call from your app or your Hoppscotch requests.
requirements.section: API Mocking > Create a mock server
requirements.statement: User can get a mock server URL after creation to call from an app or Hoppscotch requests.

requirements.quote: Delay: Add fixed or ranged latency (for example, 250-1500 ms)
requirements.section: API Mocking > Latency, errors, and headers
requirements.statement: User can add fixed or ranged latency as a delay to mock responses.

requirements.quote: You can access the collections by clicking the "Collections" icon on the side panel.
requirements.statement: User can access collections by clicking the Collections icon on the side panel.

requirements.quote: Specify the authorization, headers, and variables that all nested requests or folders should adhere to.
requirements.statement: User can specify authorization, headers, and variables for nested requests and folders in collection properties.

requirements.quote: Hoppscotch supports various variable scopes, including global, environment, and request-specific variables.
requirements.statement: User can use global, environment, and request-specific variable scopes.

requirements.quote: You can use the Set as Variable option from the context menu to assign a selected value to an environment variable.
requirements.statement: User can assign a selected value to an environment variable using the Set as Variable option from the context menu.

requirements.quote: Create global, personal, and shared environments in Hoppscotch to manage reusable variables across API requests, scripts, and workspaces.
requirements.statement: User can create global, personal, and shared environments to manage reusable variables across requests, scripts, and workspaces.

requirements.quote: Click on the "Environments" icon on the sidebar to create environments.
requirements.statement: User can open the Environments icon on the sidebar to create environments.

requirements.quote: From the dropdown menu, select Duplicate.
requirements.statement: User can duplicate an environment from the More menu by selecting Duplicate, creating a new environment with the suffix - Duplicate.

requirements.quote: However, you have the option to choose whether to sync a personal or global environment.
requirements.section: Environments > Types of Variables in an Environment
requirements.statement: User can choose whether to sync a personal or global environment.

requirements.quote: All secret variable values in Hoppscotch will be masked using asterisks (\\\*).
requirements.section: Environments > Types of Variables in an Environment
requirements.statement: User can create secret environment variables whose values are masked with asterisks and not synced to the server.

requirements.quote: You can access the history of your requests by clicking on the "History" icon on the side panel.
requirements.statement: User can open the history of their requests by clicking the History icon on the side panel.

requirements.quote: You can also delete all requests from your history by clicking on the "Clear history" button in the history section.
requirements.statement: User can delete all requests from history by clicking the Clear history button in the history section.

requirements.quote: Favorite requests can be filtered by clicking on the "Filter" button in the history section and selecting the "Favorites" filter.
requirements.statement: User can filter favorite requests using the Filter button and the Favorites filter in the history section.

requirements.quote: You can favorite a request by clicking on the "Favorite" button on the history entry's options.
requirements.statement: User can favorite a request and unfavorite it via the Favorite button in the history entry's options.

requirements.quote: To save a request to your history, you can click on the "Send" button on the request page.
requirements.statement: User can save a request to history by clicking Send on the request page, which saves it automatically.

requirements.quote: Access the Hoppscotch Web App to build, test, and share APIs directly in your browser.
requirements.statement: User can build, test, and share APIs directly in the browser using the Hoppscotch Web App.

requirements.quote: Hoppscotch also provides the capability to run Tests on the responses you receive.
requirements.statement: User can run Tests on the responses received.

requirements.quote: You can also add dynamic behaviors to your requests by specifying Headers, Request Body, Authorization Headers, Parameters, and Pre-request scripts.
requirements.statement: User can add dynamic behaviors to requests by specifying Headers, Request Body, Authorization Headers, Parameters, and Pre-request scripts.

requirements.quote: Write pre-request scripts and post-request tests in Hoppscotch using JavaScript to add dynamic behavior, set variables, and validate responses.
requirements.statement: User can write pre-request scripts and post-request tests in JavaScript to add dynamic behavior, set variables, and validate responses.

requirements.quote: Please note that only updates to request variables get persisted and reflected in the UI while the remaining are specific to the session.
requirements.section: Scripts > hopp.request Namespace > hopp.request.variables.set(key: string, value: string)
requirements.statement: User can see updates to request variables persisted and reflected in the UI, while other script updates are session-specific.

requirements.quote: In the "Tests" tab of the first API request (that returns the tokens), add the following code:
requirements.section: Scripts > pw.response > Setting Environment Variables from API Responses
requirements.statement: User can use the "Tests" tab of an API request to add code that stores response data in environment variables for use in later requests.

requirements.quote: The AI Assistant is an experimental chat assistant that can act on the request, response, environment, and collections you're working with.
requirements.statement: User can use the AI Assistant, an experimental chat assistant, to act on the request, response, environment, and collections they are working with.

requirements.quote: Validate the generated body and select Accept Change to populate the request body field.
requirements.statement: User can validate the generated body and select Accept Change to populate the request body field.

requirements.quote: Select Accept Change to integrate it into the test script editor for execution.
requirements.statement: User can select Accept Change to integrate the generated test into the test script editor.

requirements.quote: When saving an API request to a collection, click the Modify with AI icon ( .⟡+ ) next to the request name field to have the system automatically assign a name based on the request's context and properties.
requirements.statement: User can click the Modify with AI icon next to the request name field to have the system automatically name a request when saving it to a collection.

requirements.quote: Generate API documentation from your Collections
requirements.section: API Documentation > What you can do
requirements.statement: User can generate API documentation from their Collections

requirements.quote: In Hoppscotch, you can save responses as examples to quickly populate mock routes with realistic data.
requirements.section: API Mocking > Save a response as an Example
requirements.statement: User can save responses as examples to populate mock routes with realistic data.

requirements.quote: In the response section, click the "Save as Example" icon
requirements.section: API Mocking > Save a response as an Example
requirements.statement: User can click the "Save as Example" icon in the response section to save a response as an example.

requirements.quote: Right-click on a collection or a subfolder within a collection to open its properties.
requirements.section: Authorization > Managing Authorization at the Collection Level
requirements.statement: User can right-click a collection or subfolder to open its properties.

requirements.quote: You can also create a sub-collection by clicking on the "Add new" button on the desired collection and entering the name of the sub-collection.
requirements.statement: User can create a sub-collection by clicking Add new on a collection and entering a name.

requirements.quote: You can organize your collections by dragging and dropping them to the desired location.
requirements.statement: User can organize collections by dragging and dropping them to the desired location.

requirements.quote: You can also create sub-collections by dragging and dropping a collection into another collection.
requirements.statement: User can create sub-collections by dragging and dropping a collection into another collection.

requirements.quote: To add a request to a collection, click on the "New request" button on the collection's options to save the current request to the collection.
requirements.section: Collections > Organizing collections > Adding requests to collections
requirements.statement: User can add the current request to a collection with the New request button in the collection's options.

requirements.quote: Click on the drop-down menu next to the save button and click on "Save as" to save the request to a new location.
requirements.statement: User can save a request to a new location using Save as from the drop-down next to the Save button.

requirements.quote: To add a new request to your collection, you can click on the "Save" button on the request page and select the collection you want to add it to.
requirements.statement: User can add a request to a collection by clicking Save on the request page and selecting the collection.

requirements.quote: Info: The "Add to Parameters" option is available only when using query parameters.
requirements.statement: User can see the Add to Parameters option only when using query parameters.

requirements.quote: To access a request from your history, click on the desired request in the history section.
requirements.statement: User can open a request from history by clicking it in the history section.

requirements.quote: To delete a request from your history, click on the "Delete" button on the history entry's options.
requirements.statement: User can delete a request from history using the Delete button in the history entry's options.

requirements.quote: You can filter your history by clicking on the "Filter" button in the history section and selecting the desired filter.
requirements.statement: User can filter history by clicking the Filter button in the history section and selecting a filter.

requirements.quote: Right-click on the collection and select the "Run Collection" option.
requirements.statement: User can right-click a collection and select the "Run Collection" option.
